question: Does telling one bad feeling from another change how much young drinkers drink when stressed?
answer: It seems to. Young social drinkers logged their feelings and their drinking on handheld devices. Those who habitually told nervous from guilty from irritated drank about 40% less on stressful nights than those whose bad feelings blurred into one. The link comes from observation, not an experiment. A precise name points to a precise fix.
move: The finer you can name a bad feeling, the better you can answer it.
ask: When I say I feel bad, could I name which bad: tired, lonely, anxious or resentful?
reference: Kashdan, Ferssizidis, Collins & Muraven, Emotion differentiation as resilience against excessive alcohol use, Psychological Science, 2010
